title: Solving the Cold-Start Problem for the Edge: Clustering and Adaptive Deep Learning for Emotion Detection
problem: Personalized edge ML systems face cold-start problem when new users lack labeled data, and deployment constraints limit model complexity for resource-constrained edge devices.
motivation: Personalized edge AI requires addressing data scarcity for new users while maintaining privacy and real-time inference on embedded hardware.
method: CLEAR groups existing users based on their emotion-recognition patterns, finding natural clusters without needing labels (unsupervised clustering). When a new user arrives with minimal labeled data, the system assigns them to the most similar cluster and fine-tunes that cluster's model using just a few of their labeled examples, adapting it to their individual style. The entire system runs on resource-constrained edge devices: Coral Edge TPU and Movidius Neural Compute Stick 2.
key_novelty: The key idea is using unsupervised clustering to group users, allowing new users to personalize a cluster's model with just a few labeled examples instead of needing either a generic model or full individual labeling.
contributions: Clustering-based cold-start solution requiring no initial labeled data
Accuracy improvement from 75% to 81.9% via clustering
Fine-tuning achieving 86.34% accuracy on fear detection task
Efficient deployment on Coral Edge TPU and Movidius platforms

metrics.accuracy: 81.9% with clustering (vs 75% baseline), 86.34% fear detection with fine-tuning

limitations: Limited to emotion detection task on WEMAC dataset; generalization to other biosensing applications not discussed.
primary_theme: clustering-based personalization for edge emotion detection
